intro.data: You already know one route to the report: Parser then Publisher turns the raw file into THE report. From your toolkit, build a different route — through the data sample — that lands on the exact same report. Bring the Sample object and the arrows you need onto the board; one finishing machine makes a DIFFERENT report, so leave that one in the tray.
intro.alchemy: You already know one route to the alloy: Smelter then Caster turns the raw ore into THE alloy. From your toolkit, build a different route — through the powder — landing on the exact same alloy. Bring the Powder and the arrows you need onto the board; one finisher makes a different alloy, so leave it in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: You already know one route to the ward: Ignition then Weaver turns the wild spark into THE ward. From your toolkit, build a different route — through the mote — landing on the exact same ward. Bring the Mote and the arrows you need onto the board; one finisher makes a different ward, so leave it in the tray.
intro.abstract: One route A→B→C is known to produce c. From the toolkit, place object D and build the other route A→D→C that produces the SAME value c: h sends a ↦ d, then k sends d ↦ c (the finisher k′ diverges to c′ — leave it in the tray).

afterSuccess.data: Two different routes, the same report. Your sample-and-plot path produced exactly what the parse-and-publish path does — the Skewer would have produced a different report. When two routes agree on every input, the diagram commutes.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Two different routes, the same alloy. Your path produced exactly what the first one does; the Misfounder would have diverged. When routes agree on every input, the diagram commutes.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Two different routes, the same ward. Your path produced exactly what the first one does; the Twister would have diverged. When routes agree on every input, the diagram commutes.
afterSuccess.abstract: Both routes produced the same value. Two parallel routes that agree are equal — the square commutes.

reveal.summary: Different routes with the same start and end can produce the same result. When they always agree, the diagram commutes — here, checked by actually running the value.
reveal.moreFormal: Two parallel morphisms are equal when they agree on inputs. This puzzle confirms it by running the value through both routes — genuine equality, not just matching types.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Two different implementations that return the same output for the same input.
